decks.title: Topographical Maps: Settlements, Land Use, Transport and Drainage, Part 1: Settlements, land use and transport
goals: Identify settlements and the services they offer, and give reasons for the site of a settlement
Identify cultivated land, open scrub and forest and infer the occupations of the people
Identify the types of roads and tracks and the means of communication

slides.heading: What a sheet tells us about people
slides.body_md: A topographical sheet shows more than hills and rivers: it shows **where people live**, **how they use the land**, **how they move** and **where water drains**. This chapter reads all four on our **imagined practice sheet** (not a real place, not a Survey of India sheet). Part 1 is about **settlements, land use and transport**.

visual.alt: Table of the three villages of the imagined sheet and the services shown at each
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: A topographical sheet tells us about people as well as hills. It shows where they live, how they use the land, how they travel and where the water drains. In this chapter we read all of that on our imagined practice sheet. Part one covers settlements, land use and transport. Our three villages are Nandiwadi, Sonakhedi and Pathrali.

slides.heading: Where do settlements grow? The site
slides.body_md: The **site** is the exact spot where a settlement stands. Villages grow where there is **water** (stream, tank, well), **gentle, fertile land** for fields, a **road or track** for trade, and safety from floods and steep slopes. On the sheet all three villages stand on **gentle ground** (under 60 m of fall per km) near water and a track.

visual.alt: Table of the site factors of the three villages: nearest road or track, nearest water and slope, computed from the sheet
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: The site of a settlement is the exact spot where it stands. People choose a spot with water, gentle fertile land and a road or track. On our sheet all three villages stand on gentle ground. Nandiwadi and Sonakhedi are right beside the metalled road, and each has a well close by. Pathrali is near a stream and a well.

slides.heading: Three villages on the sheet
slides.body_md: In this extract you can see **Pathrali** near a stream and a well, with footpaths and an unmetalled road, and **Nandiwadi** beside the metalled road with a canal nearby. Each village is a **cluster of huts** (small black squares) with its name in bold. Look at how roads and water lie close to the huts.

visual.alt: Extract of the imagined practice sheet showing the villages of Pathrali and Nandiwadi, with the metalled road, unmetalled road, a canal and a river
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: Here are two of our villages. Pathrali stands near a stream and a well, and footpaths and an unmetalled road lead to it. Nandiwadi lies beside the metalled road, with a canal not far away. Each village is a cluster of small black squares, which are huts, and its name is printed in bold letters beside it.

slides.heading: Services in a settlement
slides.body_md: Services are shown by letters beside a small black square: **PO** (post office), **PS** (police station) and **Dis** (dispensary). A settlement with several services is a **service centre** for nearby villages. On the sheet **Nandiwadi** has a PO and a PS, **Sonakhedi** has a dispensary and **Pathrali** shows none, so Pathrali people must travel to the others.

visual.alt: Extract of the imagined practice sheet showing the huts of Nandiwadi with a post office and a police station, a well and a metalled road
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: Services are shown by letters next to a small black square. P O is a post office, P S is a police station and Dis is a dispensary. A village that has several services serves its neighbours too. On our sheet Nandiwadi has a post office and a police station, Sonakhedi has a dispensary, and Pathrali has none shown.

slides.heading: Worked example: why is Sonakhedi sited there?
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Give geographical reasons for the site of Sonakhedi.

**Step 1 (water).** A tank lies 0.78 km away and a well 0.64 km away.

**Step 2 (land).** It stands on gentle ground (26 m per km) in the middle of yellow cultivated land.

**Step 3 (communication).** The metalled road runs through it, and an unmetalled road and a cart track branch off.

**Answer.** Water supply, fertile gentle land for farming and a road link.

slides.narration: Let us give reasons for the site of Sonakhedi. First, water: a tank and a well lie within a short walk. Second, land: the village stands on gently sloping ground in the middle of cultivated fields. Third, communication: the metalled road runs through the village, with an unmetalled road and a cart track branching off. These three reasons together explain the site.

slides.heading: Land use and land cover
slides.body_md: **Land use** is how the land is used; the sheet shows it by tint. **Yellow:** cultivated land (45% of the imagined sheet). **Green:** forest (22%). **White with small green ticks:** open scrub, uncultivated land (33%). Land that is cultivated but left unsown for a season is **fallow**: this imagined sheet does not mark fallow separately. A small area of **blue** shows the tank.

slides.narration: Land use is how land is used, and the sheet shows it with tints. Yellow is cultivated land, which covers nearly half of our sheet. White with small green ticks is open scrub, about a third. Green is forest, about a fifth. Land that is farmed but left unsown for a season is called fallow, but this imagined sheet does not mark it separately.

slides.heading: Cultivated land: the people farm
slides.body_md: The low gentle ground in the south is **entirely yellow**: it is **cultivated land**. Combined with a **tank** and wells for irrigation, a canal and a **metalled road** to carry produce, this tells us that the main occupation here is **agriculture**.

slides.narration: The low gentle ground in the south is all yellow, so it is cultivated land. Add a tank, wells and a canal for irrigation, and a metalled road to carry the harvest, and the evidence points to agriculture as the main occupation here. Always link the land use to the occupation, and name the clues on the map.

slides.heading: Worked example: land use and occupations
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Infer the main occupation of people near (a) the southern plain, (b) the conical hill and (c) the western scrub.

**(a)** Yellow tint, tank, wells and canal: **farming**.

**(b)** Green tint on steep high ground with no huts: **forestry**, collecting wood and forest produce, and protection of the forest.

**(c)** White scrub with a few scattered huts and no irrigation: **grazing of animals and small dry farms**.

visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: Let us infer occupations from land use. On the southern plain the yellow tint, tank, wells and canal tell us that people are farmers. On the conical hill the green tint and the steep slopes with no huts suggest forestry. In the western scrub, a few scattered huts and no irrigation suggest grazing animals and small dry farms.

slides.heading: Quick check: land use
slides.body_md: Infer an occupation from the land use.
slides.narration: Quick check. Yellow land with a tank and a canal points to agriculture.

slides.heading: Means of transport: roads and tracks
slides.body_md: Transport is shown by lines. A **metalled road** (thick red) is the best, for all vehicles. An **unmetalled road** (thick black broken) is usable by carts and vehicles in dry weather. A **cart track** (thin black) is wide enough for bullock carts. A **pack track** (thin broken) is for animals. A **footpath** (dotted) is for people on foot. On the sheet the metalled road is about **10.9 km** long.

slides.heading: Where does the water go?
slides.body_md: Rivers follow the slope of the land. On a topographical sheet you can find the **direction of flow**, recognise the **pattern** of the streams, see whether huts are **clustered** or **dispersed**, and sort features into **natural** and **man-made**. Our imagined sheet (not a real place) shows each of these.

rows: From higher to lower: which way?
Made by nature or by people?

slides.narration: Rivers follow the slope of the land. In this part we find which way a river flows, recognise the pattern of its streams, and see whether huts are close together or far apart. Then we sort the features of the sheet into natural and man-made ones. Our imagined sheet shows examples of each.

slides.heading: Direction of flow of a river
slides.body_md: Water always flows **from higher to lower ground**. Clues: **(1)** contour values or spot heights along the river decrease downstream; **(2)** where a river crosses contours, the **V-shaped bends point upstream** (towards higher ground); **(3)** **tributaries join at acute angles pointing downstream**. On the extract, the river crosses the 140 m contour at P and the 100 m contour at Q, so it flows from P towards Q, to the **south-east**.

visual.alt: Extract of the imagined practice sheet with two points P and Q marked where the river crosses contours
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet, not a real place and not a Survey of India sheet

slides.narration: Water flows from higher ground to lower ground. There are three clues. Heights along the river fall in the direction of flow. Where a river crosses contours, the V shaped bends point upstream. And tributaries join the main river at acute angles that point downstream. Here the river crosses the one hundred and forty metre contour at P and the one hundred metre contour at Q, so it flows from P towards Q, to the south east.

slides.heading: Worked example: which way does the stream flow?
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** The stream T1 on the extract has a bed height of about 217 m at A and about 149 m at B. In which direction does it flow?

**Step 1.** Water flows to the lower end: B (149 m).

**Step 2.** B lies east of A.

**Answer.** The stream flows **from A to B, towards the east**, and joins the main river there.

slides.heading: Quick check: direction of flow
slides.body_md: Decide the direction of flow from heights.
slides.narration: Quick check. Water flows from the higher end to the lower end.

slides.heading: Drainage pattern 1: dendritic
slides.body_md: A **dendritic** pattern looks like the branches of a **tree**: tributaries join the main river from all sides at **acute angles pointing downstream**. It forms on land of fairly uniform hardness and gentle slope. The **imagined sheet** shows this pattern: the main river is joined by a tributary from the west (which has itself received a smaller tributary) and by a seasonal stream from the east, all at acute angles.

visual.alt: Extract of the imagined practice sheet showing a main river with two tributaries that join it at acute angles

slides.narration: The first pattern is dendritic, which means tree like. Tributaries join the main river from all sides at acute angles that point downstream, just like the branches of a tree. It forms where the ground is fairly uniform. Our imagined sheet shows this pattern, with a tributary joining from the west, a smaller one joining that tributary, and a seasonal stream joining from the east.

slides.heading: Drainage pattern 2: trellis
slides.body_md: A **trellis** pattern looks like a **garden fence**: long streams run **parallel** to one another and short tributaries join them at nearly **right angles**. It forms where alternating bands of hard and soft rock, or folded ridges and valleys, guide the streams. It is **not on the imagined sheet**; this is a separate schematic.

slides.body_md: In a **clustered** (nucleated) settlement the huts stand **close together** around a centre. Each village on the sheet is a cluster: the mean distance from a hut to its nearest neighbour is only about **0.09 km** in Nandiwadi. slides.heading: Dispersed settlements
slides.body_md: In a **dispersed** settlement the huts are **scattered** far apart, each among its own land. In the north-west of the sheet there are 3 huts with a mean nearest-neighbour distance of about **1.2 km**. Reasons: poor, **thinly spread land** (open scrub) that supports few people per sq km, **grazing** and dry farming that need space, and no single water source.

slides.narration: In a dispersed settlement the huts are scattered far apart. In the north west of our sheet there are three huts, more than a kilometre from one another on average. The land is open scrub that supports few people, and herders and dry farmers need space for their animals and fields. There is also no single water source to draw them together.

slides.heading: Worked example: clustered or dispersed?
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Decide the pattern of settlement in (a) Nandiwadi and (b) the north-west scrub, and give a reason for each.

**(a)** Huts about 0.1 km apart on average, around a well and a road: **clustered**; reasons: water, road and shared fields.

**(b)** Three huts with 1.2 km between neighbours, on open scrub: **dispersed**; reasons: thin land, grazing, no single water source.

slides.narration: Let us decide the pattern. In Nandiwadi the huts are about a tenth of a kilometre apart, around a well and a road, so the pattern is clustered. In the north west the huts are more than a kilometre apart on open scrub, so the pattern is dispersed. Always give the spacing as evidence and a reason for the pattern.

slides.heading: Natural and man-made features
slides.body_md: **Natural features** are made by nature: the **river**, streams, the **conical hill**, the **ridge**, the **escarpment**, forest, scrub. **Man-made features** are made by people: the **canal**, the **embankment**, the **bridge**, roads, tracks, **huts**, **wells**, the **tank** (dug and banked), the temple and the post office. A tip: if it follows a straight or smooth line that ignores the terrain, or is a building, think man-made.

slides.narration: Natural features are made by nature. On our sheet they are the river and streams, the hill, the ridge, the escarpment and the forest. Man made features are made by people. They are the canal, the embankment, the bridge, the roads and tracks, the huts, the wells, the tank and the temple. If a feature follows a smooth or straight line, or is a building, it is probably man made.

notes.title: Topographical Maps: Settlements, Land Use, Transport and Drainage: Notes

sections.heading: 1. Settlements: site and services
sections.body_md:
- The **site** of a settlement is the exact spot where it stands. Good sites have **water** (stream, tank, well), **gentle fertile land**, a **road or track**, and safety from floods.
- Services are shown by letters beside a small black square: **PO** (post office), **PS** (police station), **Dis** (dispensary).
- On the imagined practice sheet (not a real place, not a Survey of India sheet) Nandiwadi has a PO and a PS, Sonakhedi a dispensary and Pathrali none. All three villages stand on gentle ground near water and a track.

key_terms.definition_md: The exact location of a settlement and its local advantages.
A settlement whose facilities (post office, police station, dispensary) serve nearby villages.

visual.alt: Table of the services of three villages on the imagined sheet
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet

sections.heading: 2. Land use and land cover
sections.body_md:
- **Yellow:** cultivated land. **Green:** forest. **White (with small green ticks):** open scrub, uncultivated land. **Blue:** water.
- **Fallow** land is cultivated land left unsown for a season; the imagined sheet does not mark it separately.
- On the imagined sheet about 45% is cultivated, 33% open scrub and 22% forest.
- Inferring occupations: yellow land with a tank or canal suggests agriculture; green steep land with no huts suggests forestry; white scrub with scattered huts suggests grazing or dry farming.

key_terms.definition_md: The way an area of land is used, such as farming or forest.
Uncultivated land with scattered bushes and grass, shown white with small ticks.

visual.alt: Table of map evidence and the occupation it suggests
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet

sections.heading: 3. Transport and communication
sections.body_md:
- **Metalled road:** thick red line (about 10.9 km on the sheet). **Unmetalled road:** thick black broken line. **Cart track:** thin black line. **Pack track:** thin broken line. **Footpath:** dotted line.
- A **bridge** carries a road across a river. A **canal** is a blue line that follows a contour.
- Communication also includes the post office. The metalled road links Sonakhedi and Nandiwadi; the unmetalled road links Sonakhedi, Pathrali and Nandiwadi.

key_terms.definition_md: A road with a hard surface, shown in red.
A track for pack animals, shown by a thin broken line.

visual.alt: Table of the types of road and track and their symbols
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet

sections.heading: 4. Drainage: direction of flow
sections.body_md:
- Rivers flow from **higher to lower** ground: heights along the river decrease downstream.
- Where a river crosses contours, the **V-shaped bends point upstream** (towards higher ground).
- **Tributaries join at acute angles pointing downstream.**
- On the imagined sheet the main river flows south-east, falling from about 274 m to about 41 m; a tributary at A (217 m) flows east to B (149 m).

key_terms.definition_md: A stream that flows into a larger river.
Towards the source of a river, where the ground is higher.

visual.alt: Table of three clues to the direction of flow
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet

sections.heading: 5. Drainage patterns
sections.body_md:
- **Dendritic:** tree-like; tributaries join at acute angles; the pattern on the imagined sheet.
- **Trellis:** long parallel streams with short tributaries at right angles (shown here only as a separate schematic).
- **Radial:** streams flow outwards from a central high point, like the spokes of a wheel (schematic only).

key_terms.definition_md: A tree-like drainage pattern on fairly uniform ground.
A fence-like pattern of parallel streams joined at right angles.
Streams flowing outwards from a dome or conical hill.

visual.alt: Table of three drainage patterns
visual.caption: Imagined practice sheet

sections.heading: 6. Settlement patterns and natural or man-made features
sections.body_md:
- **Clustered:** huts close together (about 0.1 km apart in each village on the sheet); reasons: water, road, safety, shared fields.
- **Dispersed:** huts far apart (over 1 km in the north-west); reasons: thin land, grazing, dry farming, no single water source.
- **Natural:** river, streams, hill, ridge, escarpment, forest, scrub. **Man-made:** canal, embankment, bridge, roads, tracks, huts, wells, tank (dug and banked), temple, post office.

key_terms.definition_md: A settlement in which the huts stand close together.
A settlement in which the huts are scattered far apart.

rows: Canal, bridge, road, hut, well, tank

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Giving a one-word reason such as "water" instead of naming the source on the map.
- Naming an occupation without citing the tint, water or facilities.
- Saying a river flows uphill, or placing the V-bends the wrong way.
- Naming a pattern without describing its shape.
- Calling the tank or canal natural.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- Site (2 to 3 marks): each reason tied to map evidence.
- Land use and occupation (2 marks): the tint and the inference.
- Drainage (2 marks): direction with evidence; pattern with its shape.
- Settlement pattern (2 marks): the pattern and a reason.

questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: Name the land-use class shown by each tint on the imagined practice sheet: (a) yellow, (b) green.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Yellow shows cultivated land. (b) Green shows forest.

questions.solution_md: Cultivated land; forest.

questions.stem_md: The conical hill of the imagined practice sheet is tinted green and has no huts. Infer the likely use of the land and give one piece of evidence.

answer.model_answer_md: The hill is forest, used for forestry (wood and forest produce). The evidence is the green tint, the steep slopes shown by close contours and the absence of huts.

questions.solution_md: Forestry; green tint and no huts.

questions.stem_md: Study the extracts of the imagined practice sheet. Name the land-use class and the likely occupation in (a) the yellow southern plain, (b) the green conical hill, and (c) the white western scrub.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Cultivated land; farming (with tank, wells and canal). (b) Forest; forestry, collecting wood and forest produce. (c) Open scrub; grazing of animals and small dry farms.

questions.solution_md: Cultivated and farming; forest and forestry; scrub and grazing.

questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: Water always flows from ___ ground to lower ground.
questions.solution_md: **Higher** ground.

questions.stem_md: A tree-like drainage pattern is called a ___ pattern.
questions.solution_md: **Dendritic**.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Tributaries join the main river at obtuse angles pointing upstream.

**Reason (R):** Tributaries join the main river at acute angles pointing downstream.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: A is false. R is true — option (b).

**Assertion (A):** A radial drainage pattern forms around a dome or a conical hill.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but R describes a different pattern and does not explain A — option (d).

questions.solution_md: Outward flow from a central high point makes a radial pattern — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which of these features on the imagined practice sheet is man-made?
questions.solution_md: The canal is dug by people; the river, ridge and hill are natural — option (b).

questions.stem_md: True or false? A tank that is dug and banked by an embankment is a natural feature.
questions.solution_md: False: a dug and banked tank is man-made.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Dispersed settlements are common where the land is thin, such as open scrub used for grazing, and where there is no single water source.
questions.solution_md: True.

questions.stem_md: Cultivated land that is left unsown for a season is called ___ land.
questions.solution_md: **Fallow** land.

questions.stem_md: Huts scattered far apart, each among its own land, form a ___ settlement.
questions.solution_md: A **dispersed** settlement.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The huts of each village on the imagined sheet stand close together.

**Reason (R):** People settle near a well, a tank and a road, which gather the huts into a cluster.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and R explains A — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Give two reasons why the huts of Nandiwadi form a clustered settlement.

answer.model_answer_md: Water is available only at a few points such as the well and the canal, so people settle near them; the metalled road and the shared fields also draw the huts together; living close together gives safety and shared services (any two).

questions.solution_md: Water point; road and fields; safety.

questions.stem_md: Classify each feature of the imagined practice sheet as natural or man-made: (a) the ridge, (b) the embankment.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) The ridge is natural. (b) The embankment is man-made, built to hold the tank.

questions.solution_md: Natural; man-made.

questions.stem_md: The huts of Nandiwadi stand about 0.1 km from their nearest neighbours; the three huts of the north-west scrub stand about 1.2 km apart. (a) Name each pattern. (b) Give one reason for the first. (c) Give one reason for the second.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Nandiwadi: clustered; north-west scrub: dispersed. (b) Water points, the road and shared fields draw the huts together. (c) The land is thin open scrub supporting few people, grazing and dry farming need space, and there is no single water source.

questions.solution_md: Clustered; dispersed; two reasons.

questions.stem_md:
Study the extract of the imagined practice sheet that shows Pathrali and Nandiwadi. (a) Name the services shown at Nandiwadi. [2]

(b) Give two reasons for the site of Pathrali. [2]

(c) State the pattern of settlement in Nandiwadi and give a reason. [3]

(d) Name two means of transport that link Pathrali with other villages. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A post office (PO) and a police station (PS).

(b) It lies 0.51 km from a stream and 0.42 km from a well, so it has water; it stands on gently sloping ground close to a footpath and an unmetalled road.

(c) Clustered: the huts stand about 0.1 km from their nearest neighbours, drawn together by the well, the canal, the metalled road and shared fields.

(d) The unmetalled road and a footpath.

questions.solution_md: PO and PS; water and gentle land; clustered with reasons; unmetalled road and footpath.

questions.stem_md:
Study the sheet in which the squares P, Q and R are marked. (a) Name the land-use class of square P (4672) and of square Q (4678). [2]

(b) Name the land use of square R (4075) and the tint that shows it. [2]

(c) State the likely main occupation of the people near P, and give two pieces of map evidence from the extract of the plain. [3]

(d) Explain why few huts are found in Q. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) P: cultivated land. Q: forest.

(b) R: open scrub (uncultivated land), shown white with small green ticks.

(c) Agriculture. Evidence: the yellow tint, and the tank, wells and canal that supply water.

(d) Q is on the steep conical hill (close contours) covered by forest, where farming and building are difficult, so there are no huts.

questions.solution_md: Cultivated and forest; scrub; agriculture with evidence; steep forested hill.

questions.stem_md:
Study the extracts of the imagined practice sheet. (a) State two clues to the direction of flow of a river on a sheet. [2]

(b) The river crosses the 140 m contour at P and the 100 m contour at Q. State the direction of flow. [2]

(c) A stream bed is about 217 m high at A and 149 m at B. Calculate the fall and state the direction of flow. [3]

(d) Name the drainage pattern of the sheet and describe it. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Heights fall downstream; V-bends of contours point upstream; tributaries join at acute angles pointing downstream (any two).

(b) South-east, from P (higher) to Q (lower).

(c) Fall = 217 − 149 = 68 m. The stream flows east (from A to B).

(d) Dendritic: tree-like, with tributaries joining the main river at acute angles pointing downstream.

questions.solution_md: Clues; south-east; 68 m, east; dendritic.

(c) Name the feature that carries the metalled road over the river and state what it shows about the importance of the road. [3]

(d) Explain how roads and tracks help the villages of the sheet. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Metalled road: a thick red line. Unmetalled road: a thick black broken line (cart track, pack track and footpath are also acceptable).

(b) 10.9 ÷ 0.5 = 21.8 cm.

(c) A bridge. It shows that the road is important enough for the engineering needed to cross the river all year.

(d) They link the villages with one another and with the markets, so farm produce, goods and people can move; they give access to services such as the post office, police station and dispensary.

questions.solution_md: Metalled and unmetalled; 21.8 cm; bridge; links and services.

questions.stem_md:
Study the extracts of the imagined practice sheet and the schematic diagrams of drainage. (a) Name the drainage pattern shown on the sheet and the other two patterns in the schematic diagrams. [2]

(b) Describe the trellis and the radial patterns. [2]

(c) Compare the huts of Nandiwadi (about 0.1 km apart) with the three huts of the north-west (more than 1 km apart), naming each pattern. [3]

(d) Classify the canal, the river, the bridge and the ridge as natural or man-made, with a reason for the canal. [3]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) The sheet shows a dendritic pattern; the schematics show trellis and radial patterns.

(b) Trellis: long parallel streams joined by short tributaries at right angles, like a garden fence. Radial: streams flowing outwards from a central high point, like the spokes of a wheel.

(c) Nandiwadi has a clustered settlement (huts close together around water and the road); the north-west has a dispersed settlement (huts far apart on thin open scrub).

(d) The canal is man-made (dug by people and following a contour); the river and the ridge are natural; the bridge is man-made.

questions.solution_md: Dendritic, trellis, radial; descriptions; clustered and dispersed; natural and man-made.
